issue_paraphrase: Supplying a very large Unix timestamp, written with an @ sign in front, to the file-age filters crashes the whole program with a panic about arithmetic overflow instead of being treated like any other unparseable date input. The search aborts immediately with an unhandled panic message rather than reporting that the timestamp cannot be parsed. Any number that is well formed but simply too large to fit the internal time representation triggers the crash, so scripts that pass loosely validated timestamps die instead of receiving a parse error they could recover from.
fix_summary: In TimeFilter::from_str, `UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(timestamp_secs)` (which panics via SystemTime::Add on overflow) was replaced with `UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(...)`, so an out-of-range '@'-timestamp returns None and propagates through the existing parse-failure path (graceful '[fd error]' + exit 1). The regression test (out_of_range_unix_timestamp_is_rejected) was added in the commit immediately before the fix.
notes: Fast, fully offline after the first `cargo build` (all 130+ crates come from crates.io, resolved by the committed Cargo.lock). Debug build of fd at these commits takes roughly 1-3 minutes at 1 CPU. The parent commit chosen here (fb0426fed1) is the test-first commit, so the golden test is ALREADY present at the parent: no overlay is needed and the parent-side failure is the project's own failing test. MSRV at these commits is 1.90.0; a recent stable toolchain works (verified with 1.98.1). Note the fix applies to both --changed-before and --changed-within (same from_str path). The jiff/chrono crates have no pin needed; the lockfile governs. Verified with Ubuntu 24.04 image; no apt dependencies beyond gcc/make (installed defensively; jemalloc is not a default feature at these commits).

issue_paraphrase: When the directory a search was launched from disappears while the search is still running, the tool dies with an unhandled panic instead of finishing, skipping, or reporting the problem. The crash happens per matched file: the program tries to resolve the process's current directory for every match, hits a 'not found' result, and aborts the whole search. Launching from a directory that was already gone at startup is handled gracefully; it is the directory being removed mid-search that terminates the run abruptly.
fix_summary: Introduced a new WorkerResult::FatalError variant plus a search_str_for_entry helper that propagates path_absolute_form errors via Result instead of .expect(...) panicking. FatalError is handled in the single-command job loop, the batch path, and the receiver loop (print error if show_filesystem_errors, return ExitCode::GeneralError). Added a unit regression test that deletes the cwd and asserts search_str_for_entry returns an error.
notes: GOTCHA for the author: the upstream regression test only compiles at the fix commit (it references the helper introduced by the fix), so the parent-side failure must be produced with the CLI repro (panic + exit 101), and the fix side with either the unit test (golden) or the same CLI repro (exit 1, no panic). The CLI repro is timing-based: it needs the walk to still be active ~100ms in, so it needs a big enough tree (150k files => ~0.9s walk with -j 1 on a 64-core host; the entry paths must be RELATIVE - hence the symlinked search path inside the cwd - because absolute search paths make path_absolute_form short-circuit and never call getcwd). At parent, entries after the rmdir hit getcwd()==ENOENT => panic; observed 3/3. Do NOT overlay the fix's src/walk.rs test module onto the parent (it would double as the fix). Build is fully offline after first cargo build (~1-3 min at 1 CPU). Alternative parent trigger with same property: none found that is fully deterministic at the CLI level; keep the file count high.

issue_paraphrase: Pointing a search at a directory whose name is literally a single dash '-' silently returns no results: even though the directory exists on disk and contains matching files, the tool prints nothing and gives no error. Referencing the same directory with an explicit './' prefix works fine, so the outcome depends only on how the directory argument is spelled. Invocations that hand '-' to the tool - for example from a variable or a wrapper script - quietly produce empty output and a successful exit.
fix_summary: In Opts.normalize_path (src/cli.rs), a search-path argument equal to "-" is now rewritten to "./-" (Path::new(".").join(path)) so the underlying walker treats it as a literal path; previously "-" was passed through unchanged and the walker silently matched nothing. Added the integration test test_single_dash_root_path and a CHANGELOG entry referencing #849.
notes: Fully offline after first build. `cargo test test_single_dash_root_path` triggers compilation of the whole test suite harness (tests/tests.rs, a large file) - allow a few minutes at 1 CPU on the first invocation; afterwards it is incremental. When doing the parent-side golden run, remember the overlay is ONLY tests/tests.rs (the fix's test addition); the src/cli.rs of the parent must stay buggy, and after the run use `git reset --hard` (not `git checkout .`, which would restore the staged overlay). The CLI repro itself needs no test harness at all and is fully deterministic. The '-' directory must be created inside the temp working directory of the repro.
